source_passage_locator: K059S04: NCI Lung Cancer Prevention Health Professional Version → The Biology of Carcinogenesis; Risk Factors → Cigarette smoking; paragraph describing genetic injury as a driver of multistep lung carcinogenesis
review_note: Reviewed K059S03 and K059S04. K059S04 directly links tobacco-related genetic injury in human lung tissue with the multistep process of lung carcinogenesis. This supports DNA damage in lung cells → Increased risk of lung cancer development as RISK_FACTOR_FOR within the tobacco-related carcinogenesis pathway. K059S03 explains cancer-associated genetic alterations generally but does not independently verify the exact lung-specific relationship and remains partial. Initial DNA damage is not equivalent to a persistent oncogenic mutation. Damage may be repaired or eliminated, and lung cancer typically requires the accumulation of relevant genetic and other changes. The association is mechanistically supported but is neither sufficient nor inevitable, and no risk estimate for an individual DNA lesion is established. AI-assisted review; human confirmation pending.
